items.note: Association 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Payment by butterfat test not weight stated, but the bolded 'test of the station where he delivers governs' clause is absent.
Story 1: Article VII 'the mechanism that made everything that followed matter financially'.
Teague bookkeeper, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green; Loomis named without office. List item with no REQUIRED line, so scored on the core fact.
Section A names Selby Vose only as 'the Association's manager': no son, no 1913. The son relation appears only in B3, and D3 wrongly gives 1911.
Story 8 mentions a 'station gain' entry only in passing: no 1898 origin, no ~5.25% shape, no general account.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Weighing, composite sample, percent on the neck after a fixed charge: none of it described.
Ammon & Sons Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 7: proportionally low reading 'every time, regardless of season', explaining 'the constancy of the gap'; 0.19 given in Story 2.
Section A never says a pipette can't be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Born 1861, twenty-nine seasons from 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
No bench routine and no test-book columns or corrections practice.
3.61 appears but the 1896 figure of 3.80 is never stated in Section A. Both figures are required.
Has nine weeks, 8 May, 10 July and the question mark, but says only 'rose markedly'. The bolded 3.80 result is absent.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.
1919 circular present; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as taught, cannot say why') absent.
Died 1934 with 'the imputation on him'; test book impounded 1925, Historical Rooms 1959 (Story 8).
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Scales agreeing stated, but the start date is left unresolved among 1897/1898/1900. The bolded 1 January 1897 is not established.
Story 2 gives Hollow 3.61 vs Green 3.78 as 'a gap of about 0.19 points', conflating the visible 0.17 gap with the true 0.19 shortfall. This forfeits the item under the key.
Says the Grigg committee 'sampled the six Hessel Bottom herds through 1908'; the key has January to March 1908 only (F096 corruption).
200,000 lb at 3.42 present. Nothing in Section A says the loss was proportional so richer herds lost more; C2 actually applies a flat 0.19.
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962.
Alder Corners over Redlow Ridge and Vessey County are there, but Section A never says Jerome Cudd opened it (only Rosalie and 'the Cudd family').
Four of six Hessel Bottom farms hauled summer milk there, 1915-1930.
'Its own bench glass' plus 'corroborated independently by the factory's own records': two of the four elements.
Season averages 3.78-3.82 throughout on the same four farms' milk, against the station's 3.61.
'refuting both the watering and wet-hay theories for that milk'.
Rosalie copied the figures for Ivy in 1958, but 'daughter' is absent from Section A (appears only in E14).
Section A gives no 1907-1936 span (only the 1936 retirement). Elsewhere the run dates the circuit from 1908.
Lactometer finding is not in Section A (only D2/F).
Section A says only 'condemned in 1923': no 12 June, no burette.
Not stated that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency.
No replacement-order dates, no 1924 average of 3.80 in Section A.
Crate in station loft; notebooks to state office 1936, college library 1947 (Story 8).
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Frick's board, 17 March 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room; award four days after 30 April.
Watering, tester theft (Teague), wet hay argued; no cause established.
Four books listed including the inspector's notebook. The bolded point that it contained the answer and was read for its other lines is absent.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no cause found; $3,800 'without admission' charged to the station's own account.
One fifth of $19,000 and the charge to the accumulating 'gain' account are not in Section A.
Granddaughter, graduate student at State Agricultural College at Farland, with Vaught.
Story 8: records 'never in the same room ... until Ivy Keddie assembled them'.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
9 March 1958, 16.72 vs 17.6, about 95% of mark (0.88 not printed but ratio given).
95% stated, but Section A never gives '3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood'. No 3.80 anywhere in A.
40M lb / 76,000 lb / $19,000 / ledger identity are absent from Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cleared him; 24 years after death, 33 after 1925.
Granddaughter.
Daughter of Duncan, Ansel's son; r18 and r22 cited.
Second cousins with correct derivation.
Full vs half sister 'left open by the sources' and does not change the cousin degree.
Son of Gideon Vose.
Defending his father's Article VII payment-by-test rule.
Asserts 'the sources resolve in favor of no relationship' (A01 abstention asserted).
Treats the family denial as settling it instead of saying no document names or denies a link.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, one part in twenty.
Applies a flat +0.19 giving 3.61 and 380 lb; key is 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, 360 lb.
$95.00; key $86.40 ($90 accepted only on a correct 360 lb at 25c).
5.00% of true and 5.26% of credited, both denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
Says 'just over 26 years', not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks. Exact match fails even though 25 full years and the reason are given.
'cannot be determined precisely ... not a resolved fact'. Leans to Sill but declines, so this counts as an abstention.
Variable: the measuring glass, station's own vs borrowed.
Herds, pasture/season, tester, scales held constant.
Only 'rose markedly ... fell back'. No 3.80 or 3.61.
Cause traveled with the glass, not farms/feed/tester; limit given (mechanism/which glass not identified, borrowed glass's accuracy unknown).
Brant weigh book (r09), Strawn lactometer (r06), Alder Corners (r10): three narrators.
Independence argued; Alder Corners and lactometer hold without the 1958 measurement.
'As for the bookkeeper: no, Wilbur Teague ... apparently never questioned the ledger entries' (A09 asserted).
Yes, he knew it tested low; 1919 circular cited.
Only two valid elements (ledger sheets, 1919 circular). Gives manager from 1911, not 1913; no hearing argument or 'never names glassware' in B-G.
Claims the station-gain line was 'documentary proof' the credited/received discrepancy was known to him every year, which asserts A03. No abstention.
1924 average 3.80 vs 3.90/3.85 by arithmetic and log (row 3); Orra 1866 by r18's own age at death (row 7); 1897 vs 1898 glass start by invoice and diary.
Pairs named with breakers: $3,500 r01/r21, five dozen r11/r21, 44M r05/r12, six weeks r05/r16, eleven pipettes r12/r19, etc.
A10 declared undeterminable (minute book lost). A04 and A06 not treated as abstentions.
r11 16.27 cascade vs its own 'one part in twenty'; r18 1868 vs 82 at death in 1948; r03 Ashlin vs Larrow Green.
Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95% given, but never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80 and treats it as a flat constant (C1b additive, C2 flat +0.19). The 1896 onset at 3.80 is missing.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter, none in summer.
'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware' (A07 asserted).
Verdict sentence 'the evidence ... indicates he suspected the glass specifically from 1911 onward' (A05 asserted); later hedging doesn't undo it.
Summary is about 159 words, over the 150 limit.
Only four series named: weigh book, ledger, inspector's log, 1958 bulletin/measurement.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.
5% short, 1897, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named. Both ends covered.

Corruption: Strawn's circuit from 1908 (D2 'every circuit visit from 1908 forward', F 'from 1908 on')

Corruption: circular sent to eleven families (E15 resolved in favor of eleven) (F058)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'no relationship' (B4)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never questioned' the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: station-gain line as proof the manager knew of the understatement (D3)
Gullibility A07: board 'never examined the condemned glassware' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester 'suspected the glass specifically from 1911 onward' (F, also Story 4)
